technical_and_design_decisions: Implement in Java 17+ on Spring Framework 6 / Spring Boot, consistent with the specification baseline.

Create a new common multi-module repository (Maven/Gradle) hosting the SPI artifacts: module-registry core abstraction, receptor Admin SPI implementation, cloud-controller Admin SPI implementation, and Eureka integration (U3).

Core model: ModuleDescriptor with an immutable Key (group + name/label); ModuleStatus carrying an aggregate state enum (DEPLOYED, DEPLOYING, FAILED, INCOMPLETE, UNKNOWN) plus per-module-instance details and health attributes (U4).

Define a ModuleRegistry/Admin SPI interface exposing ModuleStatus getStatus(ModuleDescriptor), Collection<ModuleDescriptor> listModules(), and Map<ModuleDescriptor.Key, ModuleStatus> getStatus() for all modules (U1, U2).
Receptor implementation queries the Diego Receptor HTTP API (ActualLRPs/DesiredLRPs) via a lightweight REST client and maps LRP state to ModuleStatus and health metrics (U1).
Cloud Controller implementation uses the cf-java-client library to query applications and their instances, mapping CF app/instance state to ModuleStatus and health metrics (U2).

Profile awareness via Spring Boot auto-configuration with @ConditionalOnProfile/@ConditionalOnProperty and environment detection (e.g., presence of VCAP_APPLICATION) so that plain 'java -jar', 'cf push', and 'ltc create' each wire the matching implementation automatically (U5).

Eureka integration via Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka client: modules self-register on startup/install, registering under spring.application.name plus a custom logical module name and module metadata in the Eureka instance metadata map (U6, U7, U8).
Module lookup by name implemented as a metadata-backed query over the Eureka registry (DiscoveryClient/EurekaClient), supporting the custom name in addition to spring.application.name (U7).
A repository component reads Eureka metadata to determine the current state of registered modules (U8).
Testing stack: JUnit 5, Mockito, WireMock for stubbing Receptor/Cloud Controller HTTP APIs, and an embedded Eureka server for integration tests.
assumptions: A single developer performs all work; estimates are effort in work-hours, not elapsed duration.

The developer has solid experience with Spring Boot/Cloud, Cloud Foundry, and Eureka, and has access to test environments: a CF foundation with Diego/Receptor, Lattice (ltc) tooling, and a Eureka server.
Existing Spring XD Admin SPI contracts are reused where possible; the 'Possible APIs' listed in U1/U2 are indicative and may be refined during design.
No UI work is required; deliverables are libraries plus Spring Boot auto-configuration.
Health metrics are limited to what the underlying platform APIs expose (instance state, uptime, basic health indicators); no custom metrics pipeline is built.
No maintained Java client for the Receptor API is assumed, so a small dedicated REST client is included in the estimate; for Cloud Controller, the open-source cf-java-client is used.
Build tooling is a Maven or Gradle multi-module build with a simple CI pipeline (build + unit/integration tests).
Documentation scope is limited to README files, Javadoc, and short usage examples.
There is no separate QA team; the developer writes all unit and integration tests.
All third-party dependencies (Spring Cloud Netflix, cf-java-client, WireMock) are readily available from public repositories.

activities.activity_description: Analyze U1-U8, refine the SPI API surface, define the domain model (ModuleDescriptor, ModuleStatus, Key), the module decomposition, and integration approach for Receptor, Cloud Controller, and Eureka.

activities.activity_name: Common repository and multi-module build setup (U3)
activities.activity_description: Create the permanent common repository with a multi-module build (core, receptor-spi, cloud-controller-spi, eureka-integration), dependency management, and project conventions.
Configure a basic continuous integration pipeline that builds all modules and runs unit and integration tests.
Implement ModuleDescriptor, ModuleDescriptor.Key, ModuleStatus, state enums, and instance-level health/attribute model.

activities.activity_name: Module registry abstraction and default implementation (U4)
activities.activity_description: Define the ModuleRegistry/Admin SPI interface (getStatus, listModules, status map for all modules) and provide a simple default/in-memory implementation plus exception handling.

activities.activity_name: Unit tests for core registry module
activities.activity_description: Unit tests for the domain model, default registry implementation, and API contracts.
Implement a lightweight HTTP client for the Diego Receptor API, DTOs for DesiredLRP/ActualLRP, authentication/TLS handling, and error mapping.
Implement getStatus(descriptor), listModules(), and the all-modules status map by correlating LRPs to module descriptors, including health metric extraction.
Unit tests for the Receptor client and SPI implementation using WireMock-stubbed Receptor responses, including error and edge cases.
Integrate cf-java-client: connection configuration, authentication, application and instance query operations, and error handling.
Implement getStatus(descriptor), listModules(), and the all-modules status map by mapping CF applications/instances to ModuleStatus with health metrics.

activities.activity_name: Unit tests for Cloud Controller SPI
activities.activity_description: Unit tests for the Cloud Controller SPI implementation with mocked cf-java-client responses, including partial-failure and unknown-module cases.
Implement Spring Boot auto-configuration with profile/condition-based wiring so local (java -jar), cf push, and ltc create each activate the matching SPI implementation automatically.
Package the admin application and verify correct wiring in all three run modes (plain jar, cf push, ltc create) with profile resolution tests.
Implement automatic self-registration of modules with Eureka on install/startup via Spring Cloud Netflix, including registration lifecycle and configuration properties.
